notes.title: I haven't given up, okay?
notes.content:
Hello dear friends and supporters of the game. I apologize for disappearing for a while, but as you well know (I made sure you knew), I develop this game on my own and it’s non-profit (at least for now). So, over the past few months, my life has been pretty hectic because I graduated in architecture and immediately started my master’s degree (at the University of Brasília, in Brazil).

My master’s thesis is about my game. My idea is to make the entire learning process within the game scientifically validated. So, for now, there won’t be any new maps (more likely next year), and my focus will be on improving the educational side of the game—mainly by improving the texts, developing a more coherent logic, and creating a learning methodology for each architect. This kind of update isn’t the most exciting, but in the long run, it will be great for the game—believe me.

Last year, I published an academic paper about the game’s development, which you can find here: "https://sigradi.org/pt/publicacoes/". Click on the 2024 publication, download it, and search for “zeitgeist” using Ctrl+F—you’ll find the article. That way, you’ll better understand the purpose of my master’s degree, which continues from that paper.

Thanks for your patience.

notes.title: 2 New Maps - Fallingwater and Casa das Canoas
notes.content:
Hello friends, I know it’s been a while, but I’ve started working on the game alone again. I’m at the end of my architecture studies, and everything has been very hectic. I’m delighted to announce this new version, where I introduce Casa das Canoas by the great Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer and Fallingwater by architect Frank Lloyd Wright. Both projects are in beta, meaning they are not yet complete; this is just an initial experience I’d like to share with you. Casa das Canoas already includes some furniture, while Fallingwater does not have any yet. The game as a whole has seen small improvements, such as adjustments for better historical representation of the Azuma House, minor performance enhancements, and bug fixes. We are also preparing for the addition of sequential maps. This feature is already implemented in the programming, and the first architect to benefit from this process will be Tadao Ando, as a thank-you for all the game purchases in Japan. That’s all for now. I hope to bring the final or at least more polished versions of these two new works and their story mode maps soon. After that, I’ll add the other maps from architect Tadao Ando (I believe this will be quick, as the Koshino House model is already ready and adapted to Unreal).

General Updates:

Together with my advisor, we are publishing a paper on the development of the game at the SIGRADI international conference. Anyone interested in learning more is invited to read the paper at the event in Barcelona (we couldn’t secure funding to attend in person).

The game project will continue to be developed during my master’s program next year.

notes.title: We are Back!
notes.content:
Hello dear players, I know, it's been a while. As many of you know, I am now in my final year of architecture studies, so the last semester was quite hectic. Now, the team is bigger, or rather, there is now a team! My great friend Walter/Wagner, who was already helping with the game, has now officially joined the team and will be helping me with programming, which has breathed new life into the project. I had a lot of difficulty continuing to evolve the game and Wagner will be helping with that, and now the game will continuously improve in terms of usability, bug fixes, and other aspects. During this time, I wasn't idle. In fact, I did a lot, but they were very small things and I ended up not sending the update, so I will be sending here the updates related to the game in this version.

Update List:

New map and new architect: Le Corbusier and the Villa Savoye. The map is fully available and playable in both game modes. (there are still some small issues, mainly with textures, but overall the experience should be good)

Controls menu: we now have a controls menu. Not all the controls listed there are working yet, such as in the case of photo mode (which I removed due to bugs, but it will return).

Now, when reading the notes, the player can scroll down with the mouse. This allowed me to increase the font size and now there are no more notes with text overflowing at the bottom in any language (I hope).

Update in the Barcelona Pavilion, addition of flags, with physics. The grass now no longer casts shadows, which has greatly improved the performance of the Barcelona Pavilion. It is now possible to enter the project's bathroom. Cones were added to mark the map boundaries. Trees were added to the vegetation layer, along with the grass, which increased performance. Also, the movement of the grass and tree leaves was removed to increase performance.

Update in the Azuma House, we added a logo decal at the entrance of the project. We improved the lighting in the project. We corrected the house's furniture based on real images of the project. We corrected the modeling of the Azuma House.

Now, when reading all the notes, there are small figures to illustrate them. This greatly improves the way of understanding what is being said and gives more context to the notes.

We added different footstep sounds for each surface the player walks on (it's even fun to walk on the different floors now).

We updated the social media links.

We added navigation sounds in the menus and also changed the background images to make it more aesthetically pleasing.

Now, both the start screen and the loading screen show different images of various projects each time they appear on the screen.

We now have a start screen and transition animations between the menus.

The mouse now stays inside the screen and it's no longer possible to accidentally click outside the game (previously it was possible to click on other applications while in the game). The mouse also remains centered while playing.

We added a line trace. Now you can only interact by looking directly at what you want to interact with (previously it was possible to open doors while having your back to them, for example). When you can interact with the object, a small circle will appear in the center of the screen and the text at the bottom of the screen, as usual.

We added the option to crouch.

We added an option to turn on and off a flashlight directly on the player.

We added a custom cursor.

We added specific ambient sounds for each map, to increase immersion in the game.

We added sounds when interacting with curtains.

General improvement in performance across all projects and improvement in graphical quality.

Now the updates about the project. We received an honorable mention at the first prize for innovations in teaching methods at the University of Brasília (my university). Also, as I mentioned earlier, we've added a programmer to the team. I want to deeply thank you for joining the game, even though it's still in a very early stage of development. Your support has greatly helped the development of the game and I promise to bring more updates this year. Thank you very much!

Now a small roadmap of the next updates:

We will be adding the architect Frank Lloyd Wright and the Fallingwater house.

We will be adding the architect Oscar Niemeyer and the Casa das Canoas.

We will complete the story mode of the first architect, Tadao Ando (as a tribute to the great reception of the Japanese public to the game).

We will let you choose the next architect to complete their story mode.

Other small updates:

Update the surroundings of the Barcelona Pavilion, so that eternal void no longer appears.

Instead of a text to open and close doors, a small icon will appear with an animation illustrating what will be done, opening or closing doors.

We will re-enable photo mode (God willing).

We will add additional functionalities related to cars (most people really enjoyed using them), we hope to be able to add a speedometer and deformations on collision. Maybe also car-related sounds (it's more complicated than it seems).

We intend to add a function on the right mouse button to perform a panoramic zoom with autofocus (it's cooler than it sounds).

notes.title: Version 1.7.1
Addition of new languages
notes.content:
This update arrived a few days ago, but only now I had time to come here to inform you, I apologize for that. In the last update were added previous translations for the languages: Chinese (simplified), Arabic, Korean, German and Russian. They still contain several errors, I am aware of that, but I will update them little by little, as well as the 5 main languages that already existed in the game. As the goal of the game has always been the popularization of knowledge about architecture, I believe that with these new localized languages, about 80% of the plant will be able to experience the game in a language they are used to. I'd like to thank you for all the support and I'd also like to say that I'm preparing a promotion for the beginning of next month (around the 3rd or 4th), so let your interested friends know to keep an eye out.

All in all, thank you very much for all the support since the beginning, I can only thank you.

Yours truly,
Matheus Rudo

notes.title: Beginning of Tadao Ando's story mode
notes.content:
Hello, first of all, I would like to thank you for all the positive reception of the game in the last few days, it has been amazing all the feedback I have been receiving. Second, I would like to thank the receptivity to my game, but especially the Japanese receptivity. I am a great lover of Japanese architecture, I do research with themes related to it and I am very happy with this receptivity. In respect to this, I have accelerated the process of developing the story mode of the architect Tadao Ando, who is planned to be the first architect to have a full story mode. I am releasing a preliminary version right now, as well as Mies van der Rohe's, with only one map (the Azuma house). In the coming months I will be working on adding four more maps to be studied in story mode and visited in sandbox mode. I would like to inform that the whole game is made only and exclusively by me, Matheus Rudo, so the updates may take a while and the translations may not be as good as I would like. If possible leave feedback in the community (preferably in English) about the translations, it would help me a lot. I am studying Japanese, but I am still at a very beginner level. I appreciate your understanding.

Yours truly,
Matheus Rudo.

notes.title: Game release
notes.content:
I am very pleased to announce the release of my game Architecture Zeitgeist on Steam! I would first like to thank DVIZ, who supported me since the beginning of the project and helped me bring this idea to reality.

I would also like to thank my friends and professors from FAU - UnB, who gave me support and valuable feedbacks throughout the game creation process.

Architecture Zeitgeist was created with much love and dedication, aiming to popularize and make the teaching of architecture more accessible. I hope players can learn and have fun visiting and interacting with the iconic works of architecture that are present in the game.

I would like to point out that the game is still in Early Access and I am open to feedbacks and suggestions from the community. Together we can make Zeitgeist Architecture even more complete and immersive.

Once again, I thank everyone who contributed to make this dream come true. I hope everyone can enjoy the game and learn more about the fascinating art of architecture. Thank you!

I would also like to inform you that I will soon be updating the store page to add a Road Map for future updates that are on the way.

Yours truly,
Matheus Rudo
